• New electric lighting, plumbing, telephones, and other modern conveniences were installed.
• The state rooms were redecorated with the latest interior fashions and furnishings. | | **Historical Continuity & Use** | • Buckingham Palace became the main London residence and administrative headquarters for the monarch.
• It hosted royal court balls, diplomatic receptions, state visits, and national celebrations.
• The palace remained the centrepiece of the British monarchy’s public and ceremonial life—all the way through the 20th‑century upheavals (World Wars, post‑war restoration, the monarchy’s modern public outreach). | **Bottom line:** After Queen Victoria’s death, Buckingham Palace was closed for a short period of mourning, then revived under Edward VII, who presided over its first major refurbishment. Since then it has continued to function as the primary London residence of the sovereign and the epicentre of royal ceremony and state business.
